follow-up time: Until healing (mean 19 days for aspiration, 30 days for incision and drainage)
cohort: 100 women with lactational breast abscesses smaller than 5cm
finding: Needle aspiration was successful in treating 86% of lactational breast abscesses smaller than 7cm and resulted in faster healing (19 days vs. 30 days) and better cosmetic outcomes compared to incision and drainage.
mod_finding: Lower segment Cesarean section was the most common mode of delivery among participants (62%).
